clue.text: Practical demonstration of a Bikini promotion?

definitions.meaning: an example that teaches by showing rather than telling
read as '...', the aim of promoting a skimpy swimsuit is to have less clothing on

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as OBJECT (aim) and LESS ON: the goal of advertising a bikini is wearing less. The OCR noise in the held clue is not on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson taught by a concrete instance is a vivid, practical illustration of a principle.

clue.text: Bishop's position is to supervise

definitions.meaning: a bishop sits above his diocese, his see
to watch over and direct others' work

explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese, so a bishop is positioned over the see.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to watch over workers, keeping them under observation and direction.

clue.text: Nervousness jet stir could create

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be made into something new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what sets the nerves going: perhaps a jet engine stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could create' rearranges JET STIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the jitters is a colloquial way of being anxious and on edge.

clue.text: Meticulous type of government?

parts.note: a meticulous person is one who takes care, and a temporary administration holding office before an election has the same name

explanation.walkthrough: Both readings work: a careful person is a 'care-taker', and a stopgap administration is a caretaker government. The held clue's stray 'ten' is OCR noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap administration minds the shop until an election, just as a custodian looks after a building.

clue.text: Compare as to direction

parts.note: as and like both mean in the manner of
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A request to set two things side by side with regard to direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken is to point out the similarity between two things, which is comparing them.

clue.text: Can and must set out to make a study

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so the letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to arrange tins and grape juice so as to create a reading room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges CAN and MUST; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private retreat, often a person's den or study where they are undisturbed.

clue.text: Experienced sailor's Attic wit perhaps

parts.note: Attic means of ancient Athens, hence old
salt is sharp wit, as in the phrase Attic salt for refined Greek humour

explanation.surface: A seasoned seaman is known for his refined Athenian humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic salt' is a stock phrase for elegant wit; here Attic gives OLD and wit gives SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran mariner who has spent years at sea is called by this nickname.

clue.text: Island opposite to the old lost sea?

parts.note: the opposite of old is new
under the same 'opposite to', lost becomes its antonym found
under the same 'opposite to', sea becomes its antonym land

explanation.surface: An island facing an ancient sea that has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposite to' governs all three words: old, lost and sea each give their antonym.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Canadian landmass in the Atlantic is an island off the east coast of North America.

clue.text: Prince to choose gold (not at Belmont)

parts.note: to elect is to choose
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: In The Merchant of Venice a prince picks a casket; choosing the gold one was the wrong move at Belmont.
explanation.walkthrough: Belmont is Portia's house in The Merchant of Venice, where the Prince of Morocco wrongly chose the gold casket; the bracket is surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The German princes who voted for the Holy Roman Emperor held this title.

clue.text: Come after it in the next world

definitions.text: Come after it in the next world

parts.words: Come after it in the next world
parts.note: in the Lord's Prayer the word 'come' follows this word ('Thy ... come'), and the phrase with come means the afterlife

explanation.walkthrough: The Lord's Prayer has 'Thy kingdom come', and 'kingdom come' is slang for the next world.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is pictured as God's realm, and with 'come' after it the word names the afterlife.

clue.text: Flour-covered freshwater fish?

parts.note: a small river fish, the bullhead, whose folk name pictures the dusty digit of a man who grinds grain

explanation.walkthrough: The bullhead's old name comes from its flat head, likened to the thumb of a grain-grinder, which would be floury.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullhead, a small European river fish, has this traditional name from its broad flat head.

clue.text: Football examination which cannot be passed?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., a test set by the FA, England's Football Association
the quickest runner cannot be overtaken

explanation.walkthrough: The FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body; split the answer as FA'S TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever moves quickest of all can never be overtaken, as nobody goes faster.

clue.text: Game in which Miss Trent carries bat perhaps

indicators.note: Nell carries the other letters, holding them within her name

parts.note: Little Nell Trent is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word bat in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl games player is seen holding a bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop. A bat plays no part in the game, so the surface misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport played mostly by women and girls, with a ball thrown into a raised hoop.

clue.text: Serious loss of ten embarrassed employers

indicators.note: embarrassed letters are flustered into a different order
the loss of something means taking it out of the word before it

parts.note: ten written as 10 looks like the letters IO

explanation.surface: Bosses are red-faced at a serious loss of ten jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss of' removes IO from SERIOUS to leave SERUS, and 'embarrassed' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who use something put it to work, so users are employers of a tool or service.

clue.text: Less than the odd mile trek — nothing in it!

definitions.text: Less than the odd mile trek — nothing in it!

indicators.note: in tells us the zero goes inside the rearranged walk
odd suggests the words mile trek are made strange by rearranging

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A walk just short of a mile is no effort at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges MILE TREK, and 'in' puts O (nothing) inside. The whole clue also describes the answer: a distance a bit short of a mile, nothing much.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric distance of a thousand metres falls short of an imperial mile, about five-eighths of one.

clue.text: Female metalworker in Natal

definitions.note: a town in the province, not the province itself

parts.note: a lady is a woman
a smith works metal at a forge

explanation.surface: A woman blacksmith is working in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal is a former South African province, and the definition points to a town there, famous for the Boer War siege.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladysmith is a town in KwaZulu-Natal, besieged during the Boer War.

clue.text: Gave up, being left like Faith and charity?

definitions.text: being left like Faith and charity?
definitions.meaning: of the three virtues, faith, hope and charity, faith and charity are left without hope

explanation.walkthrough: The three Christian virtues are faith, hope and charity; strip out hope and you are without hope.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, which is giving up.

clue.text: Old-timer in the garden

parts.note: not an elderly gardener but an ancient garden ornament that measures hours by shadow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-timer' suggests a veteran, but it is an old device for telling the time.
explanation.definitionFit: This shadow-casting dial is a traditional way of telling time, often set on a garden pedestal.

clue.text: Listen, beer is intended for illness

indicators.note: listen asks us to hear the phrase spoken, not read it

parts.note: beer is ale; is intended means meant

explanation.surface: A warning that drinking beer is meant to make one ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen' tells you to say ALE MEANT out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor sickness or complaint.

clue.text: Actions, not always brief

definitions.meaning: containers are not always the briefcase kind

explanation.walkthrough: A brief is a lawyer's case file, so 'brief' also nods to the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawsuits are cases, and luggage boxes are cases that need not be briefcases.

clue.text: New court painter introduced as 3

definitions.note: the answer at 3 down, a custodian

indicators.note: the painter is introduced into the middle of the rearranged letters
new means made anew, so the letters of court are reassembled

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A new painter at court is introduced in the role of caretaker.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer at 3 down, a custodian of buildings, and the curator is a custodian of a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is a keeper of a museum's collection, a custodian looking after it.

clue.text: Release news of a viewer's bonus

definitions.meaning: a television set given away gratis

explanation.walkthrough: A viewer watches a TV set, so 'set free' is good news.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate a prisoner is to let them go, which is releasing them.

clue.text: Such the eclipse of Tolkien's lord?

definitions.text: Such the eclipse of Tolkien's lord?

parts.words: Such the eclipse of Tolkien's lord?
parts.note: an eclipse leaving a bright ring has this name, and Tolkien's lord is the Lord of the Rings

explanation.walkthrough: An eclipse where the sun shows a ring round the moon is described by this ring-related word; Tolkien wrote The Lord of the Rings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ring-shaped, from the Latin for a little ring.

clue.text: Kitchener Mountains

definitions.meaning: playfully, something belonging to a kitchen: a cooking stove

explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener looks like the field marshal, but it means a thing of the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen stove is a range, and a line of peaks is a mountain range.

clue.text: Give a walk-over to the old devil

definitions.meaning: to withdraw from a contest, handing the opponent a walkover

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Scratch' is a folk name for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing from a match hands victory to the opponent, and Old Scratch is a nickname for Satan.

clue.text: Hammer for the motorist

definitions.meaning: describing a cinema or restaurant served without leaving the car

explanation.walkthrough: A cinema or diner where you stay in your car is meant for motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammering a nail drives it in, and a cinema watched from cars is a drive-in.

clue.text: Meanwhile some winter immaturity

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Meanwhile, some youthful silliness in the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: In the interim means in the meantime, during the period between two events.

clue.text: Favourite to put one's shirt on?

definitions.text: Favourite to put one's shirt on?

parts.words: Favourite to put one's shirt on?
parts.note: seems to be a betting tip, a fancied runner to stake everything on, but means a frame for hanging laundry

explanation.walkthrough: To put one's shirt on a horse is to bet everything on it; here a shirt is literally hung on a drying frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden frame for airing laundry is jokingly a horse that carries garments.
